clue.text: Idiot on stone platform at end of flight

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, so the idiot word follows the stone abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
an airhead is a brainless, foolish person

explanation.surface: Some fool is standing on a stone platform at the top of a flight of steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft, but it is a flight of stairs; the landing at its top is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairhead is the landing at the top of a staircase, a platform where the flight of steps ends.

clue.text: After a short time serf gets everything

indicators.note: After places the serf word behind the short time in this down entry

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, made short
a helot was a serf or slave in ancient Sparta

explanation.surface: Following a brief spell, a peasant finally receives all he wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: HELOT, a Spartan bondsman, is a crossword favourite for serf.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the lot' is an informal idiom for the whole of something, i.e. all of it.

clue.text: I will need one egg to eat

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
an egg is O-shaped, so it stands for the letter O
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Someone announces they must have a single egg for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' at the start is not a pronoun but the definition: the chemical symbol for this element. 'will need' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the chemical symbol of the halogen element number 53 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Composer's name spoken out loud

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Composer is'

indicators.note: spoken out loud signals that the name word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a handle is slang for a person's name or nickname

explanation.surface: A musician's name is being said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-born Baroque composer of Messiah who settled in London.

clue.text: A commercial activity that restricts the game generally

indicators.note: restricts means the sale word holds in or confines the game abbreviation

parts.note: a sale is a commercial transaction
RU is Rugby Union, a game often abbreviated this way

explanation.surface: A business practice that limits a sport, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the game' could be any sport; Rugby Union is the conventional one, and 'restricts' has the sale hold it in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'as a rule' is an idiom meaning usually or in most cases, i.e. generally.

clue.text: A barn he's converted — inside's ace for dances

indicators.note: inside's means 'inside is', so the ace letter goes within the rearranged letters
converted means the letters of these words are changed into a new form, as a barn might be converted

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A man has done up an old barn as a home, and an ace is now living in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges A BARN HES; 'inside's' (inside is) adds A, for ace, within those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Habaneras are slow Cuban dances in duple time, the most famous being from Bizet's Carmen.

clue.text: Unwise one going over limit with cop around

indicators.note: going over in a down entry means the one letter sits above the rest

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: around signals the limit and cop letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rash person exceeds the speed limit with a policeman nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over limit' reads as speeding, but 'going over' only puts I on top in this down entry, and 'around' is the signal to rearrange the remaining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolitic is a synonym for unwise or imprudent, describing a course that is tactless or ill-judged.

clue.text: Tutor not one to criticise convert

indicators.note: not means the one letter is left out of the tutor word

parts.note: to train someone is to tutor or coach them
the Roman numeral for one is I
to slate is to criticise harshly, a British usage

explanation.surface: A teacher should avoid finding fault with a new convert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' tells you to drop I from the tutor word; to slate is British for to criticise severely.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to convert words from one language into another, a verb synonym.

clue.text: In basket male displaces power tool

indicators.note: displaces means the male letter takes the place of the power letter

parts.note: a hamper is a large basket, often for picnic food
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: In a basket, a man's tool replaces a power tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power tool' reads as a single phrase, but 'power' is P and 'tool' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammer is the commonest hand tool, used for driving in nails.

clue.text: Nose about, taking notice, about to get close to listen

indicators.note: about means the nose word is turned round

parts.note: neb is a dialect word for a nose or beak

indicators.note: the second about turns the notice word round in the same way

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
near means close by

explanation.surface: Someone pokes about, paying attention, ready to come close and hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' appears twice and each one turns its own piece: NEB becomes BEN, AD becomes DA. 'to get' is a link, and 'to listen' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend an ear is an idiom for listening attentively to someone.

clue.text: Car a learner will get in before long

indicators.note: get in means the a and learner letters go inside the before-long word

parts.note: soon means before long
L is the learner symbol, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars

explanation.surface: A learner driver will be getting into a car soon.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates, red L on white, mark a learner driver's car in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saloon is the British term for a sedan, a car with a closed body and separate boot.

clue.text: Gathered in and accounted for at a higher level

definitions.meaning: collected together, as stock or suspects are herded up

definitions.text: accounted for at a higher level
definitions.meaning: a number taken to the next whole figure above it

explanation.definitionFit: Rounded up means both herded together and, of a figure, raised to the next whole number.

clue.text: Excusable, as an evil could be

indicators.note: could be signals these letters might form another word once rearranged

explanation.surface: An excuse is made for some wrongdoing, as a minor evil might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges AN EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Venial describes a sin or fault that is pardonable, i.e. forgivable rather than grave.

clue.text: Lacking strikers beyond compare?

definitions.meaning: without the sticks one strikes to make a flame

explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means unequalled, and read whimsically it means having no matches to strike.

clue.text: Rushed from steep slope before break of day

parts.note: a scarp is a steep slope or escarpment
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: break of here means the first letter, the very start, of the day word

explanation.surface: Someone hurried down a steep hill ahead of dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break of day' looks like dawn but gives just its first letter, D. Scarper is British slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for running off hastily, so rushed away is the sense.

clue.text: The first man to get religion as a singer

parts.note: in the Bible Adam was the first man
a faith is a religion

explanation.surface: The first human gains religion as a singer would.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Faith was a British pop singer of the late 1950s and 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Faith was an English pop singer, a teen idol famous for the hit 'What Do You Want?'.

clue.text: Bill is in a state in America

explanation.definitionFit: Neb is a dialect word for beak and also the abbreviation for the US state of Nebraska.

clue.text: Game with cards face up

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the face word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pan is slang for a face

explanation.surface: A card game is played with the cards turned face upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face up' reads as how cards lie, but PAN is the face, turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap, short for Napoleon, is a trick-taking card game like whist.

clue.text: Fight in the wood

definitions.meaning: to spar with fists in the ring
the hard timber of a shrub used for carving

explanation.definitionFit: To box is to fight with fists, and box is also the dense timber of the box tree.

clue.text: Song about in idyllic location

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Song about in idyllic location': ARIA must go round CAD, but no word in the clue as held gives CAD, so a word (such as 'cad' or 'bounder') appears to be missing.

clue.text: I'd eat no stew, following an eating plan

indicators.note: stew means these letters are mixed together, as ingredients are in a stew

explanation.surface: Someone refuses stew because they are watching their weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like a dish, but it rearranges I'D EAT NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a diet means keeping to a restricted eating plan, often to lose weight.

clue.text: Reportedly tries to open 18

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 18 down, a container

indicators.note: Reportedly signals the word sounds like the one heard

parts.note: picks a lock means tries to open it without a key

explanation.surface: Someone, it is said, attempts to open a box.
explanation.walkthrough: A pyx is the box in which consecrated bread is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyx is a small container, a vessel holding the consecrated Host in church.

clue.text: Dane you found wandering around in the capital

indicators.note: found wandering around pictures the letters roaming into a new order

explanation.surface: A Dane you came across roaming about in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' just links; YAOUNDE is the capital of Cameroon.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaounde is the capital city of Cameroon in central Africa.

clue.text: At back of church see plate

indicators.note: At back of places the see word behind the church abbreviation

parts.note: the Holy See is in Rome, the Pope's see

explanation.surface: At the rear of a church one can see a collection plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not a verb but a bishop's seat; Rome is the Pope's.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium plate, a shiny metallic coating on car trim and fittings.

clue.text: Chemical leaking from receptacle then explodes

indicators.note: leaking from means letters seep out of the words, found inside them

explanation.surface: A substance seeps out of a container which then blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethene, also called ethylene, is a gaseous hydrocarbon, a simple organic compound.

clue.text: Who possibly gets caught in entrance?

indicators.note: in means the caught abbreviation goes inside the entrance word

parts.note: a door is an entrance
ct is a cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Who is it that gets trapped in a doorway?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' is not a question word but the Time Lord of Doctor Who, the BBC science-fiction series; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Time Lord hero of the BBC series is known as the Doctor, so 'Who' suggests him.

clue.text: Items of food served up — one's dropped in passage

indicators.note: dropped in means the one letter is put inside the turned food word
served up in a down entry means the food word is read upwards

parts.note: tarts are pastry items of food
the Roman numeral for one is I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Pastries are brought to the table, but one falls in the corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns TARTS to STRAT, and 'dropped in' puts I within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow sea passage joining two larger bodies of water.

clue.text: Away from home, couple run into that American city

indicators.note: into means the couple and run pieces go inside the away word

parts.note: to go forth is to set out away from home
a couple is two
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Travelling, a pair dash into that US city.
explanation.walkthrough: TWO and R go into FORTH; 'that' just points at the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Worth is a large city in Texas, next to Dallas.

clue.text: Wonder about entering grassland to find room to play

indicators.note: entering means the turned wonder word goes inside the grassland word

parts.note: a ley is land temporarily under grass

indicators.note: about means the wonder word is turned round

parts.note: awe is a feeling of wonder

explanation.surface: Feeling amazed while strolling into a meadow where there is space to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the wonder word round, giving EWA; a ley is a field temporarily sown with grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is margin or scope for freedom of action, i.e. room to manoeuvre.

clue.text: Inherited article right inside rambling castle

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: inside means the right letter goes within the rearranged castle letters
rambling describes the castle letters as sprawling about into a new shape

explanation.surface: A heirloom with its rights is kept within a sprawling family castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' rearranges CASTLE, and 'inside' puts R within to make CESTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral means passed down from ancestors, so inherited is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Secret language that's heard in place of refuge

indicators.note: that's heard signals the refuge word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a shelter is a place of refuge

explanation.surface: A coded tongue is overheard in a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelta is the cant or secret jargon used by Irish Travellers.

clue.text: Lion's speed crossing the heart of Tibet

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Lion is'

indicators.note: crossing means the speed word stretches across, containing, the central letter

parts.note: celerity means swiftness or speed

indicators.note: the heart of means the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A big cat moves swiftly across the middle of Tibet.
explanation.walkthrough: A lion is a famous person, as in 'literary lion'; the big cat is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A social lion is a much-feted person, a famous figure everyone wants to meet.
